title: Why We Read Poems
text:
Poetry uses rhythm, rhyme, and carefully chosen images to express feelings in a small space. Unlike a long novel, a poem often asks the reader to slow down and think about each word. Many poets use metaphors, which compare two things without using the words 'like' or 'as'. Because of this, a single poem can have several meanings.

Students who study poetry often find that it improves their reading skills. In a poem, the most important ideas are sometimes hidden between the lines. Therefore, readers must look for clues in the title, the rhythm, and the repeated words. Although poetry can seem difficult at first, practice makes it easier to understand.

options: Poems are always shorter than they look

questions.text: What can be inferred about students who regularly practice reading poetry?
options: They will always understand every poem at once
They will likely become more confident readers
They will no longer need to read carefully
They will be able to write novels faster

paragraph_translations: La poesía utiliza el ritmo, la rima y las imágenes cuidadosamente elegidas para expresar sentimientos en un espacio pequeño. A diferencia de una novela larga, un poema a menudo pide al lector que reduzca la velocidad y piense en cada palabra. Muchos poetas usan metáforas, que comparan dos cosas sin usar las palabras 'like' o 'as'. Por eso, un solo poema puede tener varios significados.

Los estudiantes que estudian poesía suelen descubrir que esto mejora sus habilidades de lectura. En un poema, las ideas más importantes a veces están ocultas entre los versos. Por lo tanto, los lectores deben buscar pistas en el título, en el ritmo y en las palabras repetidas. Aunque la poesía puede parecer difícil al principio, la práctica facilita su comprensión.
